summary: This lecture discusses a hadith about the two types of people worthy of envy in Islam: those who possess knowledge of the Quran and Sunnah and implement it, and those who have wealth and spend it generously for the sake of Allah. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that this type of envy is positive—wishing to have what others possess—rather than destructive jealousy. The lecture explores the concept of hikma (wisdom) as deep understanding of Islamic texts and their implementation, explaining that the Sunnah represents the Prophet's prophetic understanding of the Quran. Sh. Ali Mashhour illustrates through historical examples of Sahaba (companions) how they spent their entire wealth for Allah's sake, contrasting their commitment with modern Muslims' reluctance to make similar sacrifices. The talk challenges contemporary attitudes toward extreme generosity in deen versus worldly matters.
suggested_title: Two Types of People Worthy of Envy: Knowledge and Charitable Spending in Islam
catchy_title: Who deserves your envy in Islam?
